positions.stance: "Gentrification of housing in my district."
"The city is facing a significant, worsening shortage of affordable housing, with the Mid-Ohio Regional Planning Commission (MORPC) projecting a population of 3 million by 2050."
"Better relationship with our police force."
"Homelessness and opioid addiction rehab."
"Property taxes and home improvement grants."

H2OH03125.name: Joyce Beatty
H2OH03125.bio: U.S. Representative for Ohio's 3rd District since 2013; former Ohio House Democratic leader and Ohio State University senior vice president.

positions.stance: Supports legislation ensuring every Central Ohioan can earn a livable wage, equal pay for equal work, and more investment in workforce training and education.
Fighting to reduce the cost of college, increase investment in public schools, address the student loan debt crisis, and expand access to STEM fields.
"Healthcare is a right, not just a privilege for the financially fortunate"; supports expanding and strengthening the Affordable Care Act.
Supports expanding Social Security, Medicare, and Medicaid, and strengthening these programs to ensure their long-term solvency.
Working to address unequal pay, sexual harassment, and threats to "a woman's right to choose and access to birth control."

H2OH15228.name: Mike Carey
H2OH15228.bio: Mike Carey is the U.S. Representative for Ohio's 15th Congressional District; before that, he served as a military officer and spent more than 20 years as an executive at an Ohio-based energy company.

positions.stance: Says his top priority is "strengthening Ohio communities by promoting economic growth, public safety, and opportunity for working families," including bringing federal funding back to local projects.
Says he is working to lower living costs by "reducing taxes, creating good-paying jobs, and fighting inflation," citing the Working Families Tax Cuts law, including no taxes on tips or overtime.
Says he is "committed to strengthening Social Security and ensuring seniors receive the benefits they have earned," including fixing Social Security Administration overpayment notices.
Says he "supports law enforcement, secure borders, and policies that keep Ohio families and neighborhoods safe," citing his votes for the Laken Riley Act and the HALT Fentanyl Act.
Says veterans, law enforcement, and first responders "deserve the respect, resources, and care they've earned," citing bills that support EMS grants and health savings accounts for veterans.

oh-ag-2026-faber-keith.name: Keith Faber
oh-ag-2026-faber-keith.bio: Keith Faber is Ohio's 33rd Auditor of State, a former President of the Ohio Senate, and has a private law practice in Celina, Ohio.

positions.stance: Keith says he will stand up for constitutional rights, protect religious liberty, and defend Ohio against federal overreach by unelected bureaucrats, working alongside President Trump.
Keith says he will reduce demand through addiction treatment, prosecute suppliers, cut off supply chains at the border, and support recovery efforts for victims.
Keith says he will protect consumers from fraud, scams, and unfair business practices, and increase enforcement against predatory companies and cybercriminals, especially those who target seniors.
Keith says he will work with partners to identify trafficking networks and prosecute offenders, and expand survivors' access to recovery services, safe housing, and job training.
Keith proposes a Health Insurance Denial Resolution Program in the Attorney General's office to educate and assist Ohioans in appealing medical claim denials and to intervene with insurers.

oh-ag-2026-kulewicz-john.name: John J. Kulewicz
oh-ag-2026-kulewicz-john.bio: John J. Kulewicz is a lawyer who worked as a litigator in Columbus for over 40 years and has served on the Upper Arlington City Council since 2020.

positions.stance: He says getting back to basic issues means "taking on corrupt politicians."
He says getting back to basic issues means "restoring transparency and accountability to our government."
He says getting back to basic issues means "taking on price-fixing monopolies."
He says the job means taking on "scam artists and robocallers" and "anyone else trying to rip us off."
He says the job means taking on "Medicaid provider and nursing home fraudsters."

oh-app10-2026-0701-jamison-terri.name: Terri Jamison
oh-app10-2026-0701-jamison-terri.bio: Terri Jamison is a judge on the Ohio Court of Appeals, Tenth Appellate District, and previously served as a judge in the Franklin County Domestic Relations-Juvenile Branch; she has also worked as a coal miner, an insurance agency owner, an attorney in private practice and a state hearing officer.

positions.stance: She says "a judge should not be swayed by public opinion nor campaign contributions."
She starts by looking at "the original intent or original meaning of the rule at the time it was created" and at what legislators intended.
"I will apply the law to the individual facts of the case and to our current society to ensure justice and equity for all people."
She believes that when no rule fits the facts, a judge has the authority to interpret the law and decide questions of public or great general interest.

oh-aud-2026-blackwell-annette.name: Annette Blackwell
oh-aud-2026-blackwell-annette.bio: Annette Blackwell is the Mayor and Safety Director of Maple Heights, Ohio, and previously held private-sector jobs at KeyBank and University Hospitals and spent 16 years specializing in property tax at Deloitte and Ryan.

positions.stance: "Root out the corruption plaguing Ohio's government"
"Safeguard taxpayer dollars"
"Stand against the endless raid of local government funds by Statehouse politicians"
"As a member of the redistricting commission, fight for fair representation"

oh-aud-2026-larose-frank.name: Frank LaRose
oh-aud-2026-larose-frank.bio: Frank LaRose is Ohio's 51st Secretary of State, a former Ohio state senator, and a U.S. Army veteran and Green Beret who serves in the Ohio National Guard.

positions.stance: As Auditor, he says he will "help state and local government offices across Ohio more openly and efficiently manage our tax dollars and hold them accountable when they don't."

oh-franklin-2026-auditor-stinziano-micha.name: Michael Stinziano
oh-franklin-2026-auditor-stinziano-micha.bio: Michael Stinziano is the Franklin County Auditor and an attorney. He previously directed the Franklin County Board of Elections, served in the Ohio General Assembly and on Columbus City Council, and teaches as an adjunct professor at Capital University Law School.

positions.stance: Says "the best ideas come directly from residents"; he holds weekly Community Hours meetings and removed the Auditor's office fee for name changes on county documents.
Expanded consumer protection with a fraud protection hotline and works on title fraud through an e-alert system and with law enforcement.
Says he has made the Auditor's office more transparent and accessible by giving consumers more information, updating real estate search tools, and offering more forms online.
Supports expanding Ohio's Homestead Exemption Program for low-income seniors and disabled Ohioans, and "will continue to advocate for common sense Property Tax reform."
Supports a transparent, accessible triennial review process so community growth does not displace people from their property, and educates owners about their role in valuations.

oh-franklin-2026-commissioner-0101-crawl.name: Erica C. Crawley
oh-franklin-2026-commissioner-0101-crawl.bio: Erica C. Crawley is a Franklin County Commissioner and former state representative who served in the U.S. Navy and advocated for children and families with Cuyahoga County Job & Family Services and other organizations.

positions.stance: As Commissioner, Crawley says she is "enhancing the focus around maternal and infant health initiatives" by working with CelebrateOne, ROOTT, grassroots organizations and the federal government.
As Commissioner, Crawley says she is "working to create a health equity and outcomes policy advisor position who will work with every level of government."
Crawley says she is "fighting to ensure our policies support our children and families, especially to create pathways out of poverty and reduce criminality."
Crawley says she supports more job training services and after-school programs so that everyone in Franklin County has an opportunity to earn a living wage.
As Commissioner, Crawley says she "advocates for green energy policy and building standards at the county level."

oh-franklin-2026-cpdr-0102-boller-kelley.name: Kelley Gabrielle Boller
oh-franklin-2026-cpdr-0102-boller-kelley.bio: Kelley Boller is a family law attorney in Franklin County, Ohio, who founded her own domestic relations law firm; she was previously a staff attorney with Columbus Legal Aid Society's Family Law Unit and managed Hamilton County Juvenile Court's Family Recovery Court, Mental Health Court, and Mediation programs.

oh-franklin-2026-cpgen-0702-brown-chris.name: Chris Brown
oh-franklin-2026-cpgen-0702-brown-chris.bio: Chris Brown has served as a judge on the Franklin County Court of Common Pleas, General Division, since 2015, and before that worked as a Franklin County assistant prosecutor in the Special Victims Unit and as a private criminal defense attorney.

positions.stance: If re-elected, he says he "will continue to vigorously apply the law to each case, with an eye towards the intent and the impact of the law on all people."

oh-franklin-2026-probate-0209-green-kell.name: Kelly Green
oh-franklin-2026-probate-0209-green-kell.bio: Kelly Green is the Chief Magistrate of the Franklin County Probate Court.

oh-franklin-2026-probate-0209-junga-chri.name: Chris Junga
oh-franklin-2026-probate-0209-junga-chri.bio: Chris Junga is an attorney with more than 25 years of legal experience who has represented clients in criminal, civil, and probate cases and has led public defender offices.

oh-gov-2026-acton-amy.name: Amy Acton
oh-gov-2026-acton-amy.bio: Amy Acton is a doctor who has been a professor of maternal and child health and global public health at Ohio State University, worked at the Columbus Foundation, and served as Director of the Ohio Department of Health.

positions.stance: Her "number one priority" as governor is a Working Families Tax Cut, including an Earned Income Credit and a child tax credit for families earning up to $85,000.
On day one she would issue anti-corruption executive orders, create an Anti-Corruption Task Force, close the revolving door in appointments, and expand disclosure and transparency.

She would restore public school funding, implement the Fair School Funding Plan, reform the school voucher system, and push for free school breakfast and lunch; "Public money should be for public schools."
She would protect Medicaid and Medicare, start an Ohio Rx platform to lower drug prices, require clearer insurance and hospital pricing, and work to relieve medical debt.
She would order a full review of JobsOhio requiring more transparency and accountability, and focus on small businesses, workforce training, and infrastructure such as broadband and transportation.
Says data centers are becoming part of a surveillance infrastructure, use large amounts of electricity and water, and often get special tax incentives while residents pay higher utility costs.
As Governor, would work with the General Assembly to restrict or prohibit government use of automated license-plate surveillance systems and limit sharing of vehicle-location data.
"We are in favor of the end property tax amendment." Prefers local consumption-based funding and ending corporate welfare.
Wants to end corporate contributions from regulated monopolies, ban legislators from lobbying for 5 years after office, and put government contracts and budgets in a searchable public database.
Wants a more collaborative small business ecosystem and simpler licensing and regulation for gig workers, tradespeople, in-home childcare and other local entrepreneurs.

oh-gov-2026-ramaswamy-vivek.name: Vivek Ramaswamy
oh-gov-2026-ramaswamy-vivek.bio: Vivek Ramaswamy's campaign site calls him a business leader who has built companies, including companies developing medications.

positions.stance: Ramaswamy says he would "Slash property taxes immediately" and phase out the state income tax, starting by eliminating capital gains taxes.
He would raise academic standards, give parents more transparency and choice, pay the best teachers more, and expand career-technical education and apprenticeships.
He would "Enforce stricter bail and sentencing" for repeat violent offenders, give local police and sheriffs more power, and address severe psychiatric illness.
He says he will bring people together around shared values, not partisan divides, and restore a political culture where people can respectfully disagree.
He pledges that nearby residents would pay nothing for home electricity and lower property taxes, and that data centers would meet air and water standards, or not be built.

oh-hd01-2026-greff-joel.name: Joel A. Greff
oh-hd01-2026-greff-joel.bio: Joel Greff's campaign site calls him a businessman and community leader who lives in Bexley and holds degrees from The Ohio State University and Franklin University (MBA).

positions.stance: Says Ohio needs to keep attracting and creating more jobs for Ohioans, and that startups and small businesses can open more opportunities.
Wants schools to teach financial and technology literacy, to "double-down on growing our skilled trades programs," and to go beyond meeting State standards.
Says rents, utilities and food costs are rising faster than income and local taxes are pushing residents out; calls to "get fiscal accountability back to Main Street."

oh-hd02-2026-king-charity.name: Charity Martin King
oh-hd02-2026-king-charity.bio: Charity Martin King describes herself as a community leader, consultant, and strategist with over 30 years of experience in business development, workforce alignment, education, and community initiatives.

positions.stance: She says "access to jobs, affordable daycare, reliable transportation, and support for small businesses are essential" and backs policies that expand career pathways and support local entrepreneurs.
She supports reducing barriers to mental and physical health care and "investing in clean water and sustainable energy" to support public health, jobs, and the environment.
She supports "innovative and responsible development strategies that expand affordable housing options" so residents have safe, secure, and sustainable housing.
She supports strengthening community partnerships, building residents' skills, and "expanding transit options and improving infrastructure" to connect District 2 residents to jobs and services.

oh-hd03-2026-kent-bernadine.name: Bernadine Kennedy Kent
oh-hd03-2026-kent-bernadine.bio: Bernadine Kennedy Kent is a former two-term Ohio State Representative from parts of Columbus who previously worked as a teacher and as an advocate helping families navigate public systems.

positions.stance: She says government should answer "to the people—not insiders, not special interests," and pledges to fight corruption and waste, increase transparency in state agencies, and protect taxpayer dollars.
She pledges to "Strengthen child protection laws," "Support parents and families," and "Improve school accountability."
She says "Safe communities start with strong leadership" and pledges to support law enforcement, address root causes of crime, and protect neighborhoods and families.

oh-hd04-2026-piccolantonio-beryl.name: Beryl Brown Piccolantonio
oh-hd04-2026-piccolantonio-beryl.bio: Beryl Brown Piccolantonio is the State Representative for Ohio House District 4. She has worked as a lawyer for the state of Ohio for more than 20 years and served eight years as president of the Gahanna-Jefferson school board.

positions.stance: She believes "a woman has the right to make her own decisions about her body, her health, her family" and supports the Ohio constitutional amendment protecting that right.
Her pledge is "to work to make our state a place where young people choose to stay," with many opportunities to work, thrive and succeed.
She is committed to making sure every Ohio student can get a high quality education, no matter where they live.
"Growth is good, but smart growth is even better." She will work to make smart decisions and wise investments as the area's economy and jobs grow.
She supports an effort to end gerrymandering in Ohio by letting citizens draw fair districts. She also calls for elected leaders with strong ethical standards.

oh-hd06-2026-cockley-christine.name: Christine Cockley
oh-hd06-2026-cockley-christine.bio: Christine Cockley is the State Representative for Ohio House District 6. She previously worked as a private-sector human resources specialist, worked for YWCA Columbus and worked in government.

positions.stance: Supports targeted property tax freezes, a larger homestead exemption, public-private partnerships for affordable housing development and "holding out-of-state investors accountable."
Supports investing in childcare providers and growing their workforce, and says more families should qualify for publicly funded childcare.
Supports "commonsense safeguards on the use of price-setting algorithms" and stronger utility billing transparency on fees, rate increases and charges.
Supports fair funding for public education and minimum teacher salaries, and wants more teachers, counselors and administrators to enter the profession.
Wants wider access to higher education, more affordable college, less student debt and more support for public colleges, and says skilled trades are critical to Ohio's future.

oh-hd06-2026-jackson-matthew.name: Matthew Jackson
oh-hd06-2026-jackson-matthew.bio: Matthew Jackson describes himself as a military veteran and Fire EMS professional, with a background in firefighting, AEMT and Navy service.

positions.stance: Lists "Safe Communities" as one of his key priorities. The site gives no further detail.
Lists "Lower Taxes" as one of his key priorities. The site gives no further detail.
Lists "School Choice" as one of his key priorities. The site gives no further detail.
Lists "Affordable Housing" as one of his key priorities. The site gives no further detail.
Lists "Support Veteran Services" as one of his key priorities. The site gives no further detail.

oh-hd07-2026-jeter-ukeme.name: Ukeme Awakessien Jeter
oh-hd07-2026-jeter-ukeme.bio: Ukeme Awakessien Jeter is the current Mayor and Council President of Upper Arlington, and her campaign site also describes her as an engineer, a lawyer, a working mom and an immigrant.

positions.stance: She says she "will fight for fair, constitutional school funding so homeowners finally get real, lasting tax relief."
She says she will push back against unfunded mandates and support state investment in housing, lower childcare and energy costs, small businesses and aging infrastructure.
She says she "will fight to stop the voucher drain, reinvest in public education, and ensure teachers and students have the resources they need to succeed."
She says she "will work with anyone who is serious about getting things done" and will focus on results for families, seniors and small businesses in District 7.

oh-hd07-2026-koffel-cameron.name: Cameron Koffel
oh-hd07-2026-koffel-cameron.bio: Cameron Koffel works in criminal defense.

positions.stance: Would cap property tax on owner-occupied primary homes at a percentage of household income, with the state paying for it by ending the data center sales tax exemption. Opposes total abolition.
Would update school funding formula cost inputs every year in state law, fix the local share calculation, and require the state to publish funding shortfalls before levy votes.
Would "Codify the 85% take-or-pay standard statewide," end the data center sales tax exemption, and require utilities to list data-center-driven costs separately on bills.
Supports permit deadlines, third-party plan review, and a statewide library of pre-approved plans. Opposes the state overriding local zoning in Upper Arlington or Grandview.
Supports requiring a warrant to search historical license plate reader data, a retention limit set in law, audited searches, limits on out-of-state sharing, and penalties for misuse.

oh-hd07-2026-mercier-william.name: William Mercier
oh-hd07-2026-mercier-william.bio: Bill Mercier is a Senior Consultant for Technical Services and Aviation Operations who consults with the Pentagon and airlines, and he previously worked as a legislative aide to Ohio House Speaker Jo Ann Davidson.

positions.stance: "Partner with Law Enforcement for safer neighborhoods, responsible policing and strong communities."
"Parents should have a voice. Educators should have resources and support to be successful. Every child MUST have the opportunity to succeed"
"Build the Central Ohio economy of tomorrow with a reasonable tax structure for today."
"Fix what's broken and measure results. Stop wasting Ohioans' money."

oh-hd08-2026-somani-anita.name: Anita Somani
oh-hd08-2026-somani-anita.bio: Anita Somani is the State Representative for Ohio's 8th House District and has worked as an obstetrician and gynecologist in Columbus for more than 30 years.

positions.stance: Says "healthcare decisions should be made by patients and their doctors" and pledges to work on lower costs, reproductive freedom, IVF access, and prescription drug prices.
Pledges to keep "fighting for fair school funding" and to oppose efforts to divert taxpayer dollars away from public schools.
Supports lowering health insurance premiums and prescription drug costs, helping families afford childcare and housing, and transparency instead of hidden fees for consumers.
Pledges to protect reproductive freedom, defend the rights of LGBTQ+ Ohioans, and safeguard the right to vote, saying government should stay out of personal decisions.
Supports first responders, investment in public health and mental health, and "reducing gun violence through commonsense policies," with a focus on prevention.

oh-hd09-2026-abdullahi-munira.name: Munira Yasin Abdullahi
oh-hd09-2026-abdullahi-munira.bio: Munira Abdullahi has spent about ten years working with local nonprofits on youth development, leadership, and community service, and she has been an IGNITE National Fellow.

positions.stance: She says "healthcare is a human right" and supports lowering prescription drug costs, capping prices on life-saving medications, expanding Medicaid, and Medicare for All.
She says "Every child deserves access to quality education" and supports higher educator salaries, support for students with disabilities, school renovations, and free mental health services.
She supports more access to micro-loans, loans, and grants, resources for minority entrepreneurs, and workers' rights, including collective bargaining and union protections.
She supports the Green New Deal, investing in wind and solar, switching COTA buses to renewable energy, and repealing House Bill 6.
She supports ending redlining and unfair housing practices, rent relief for low-income residents, help for first-time homeowners, more shelters, and investment in affordable housing.

oh-hd10-2026-d-angelo-denise.name: Denise D'Angelo
oh-hd10-2026-d-angelo-denise.bio: Denise D'Angelo has run a massage therapy practice in Grove City since 2005 and has served on the South Western City School Board since she was elected in 2023.

positions.stance: She will fight to make education funding follow the student, so every parent can choose "public, private, or homeschool" for their child.
She is committed to ending the "perpetual rent" of property taxes so that no family or senior is taxed out of their own home.
She will bring a "mom's eye" to the state budget and demand that every dollar spent is visible and every legislative decision is made openly.

oh-hd10-2026-sigrist-mark.name: Mark Sigrist
oh-hd10-2026-sigrist-mark.bio: Mark Sigrist is the state representative for Ohio House District 10. He previously served as an at-large member of the Grove City Council and worked at Honda North America, where he was an executive.

positions.stance: He says the state needs to make senior care a priority and wants to "find solutions that help them age safely in their homes."
He wants to focus on adding affordable housing near workplaces, along with "more accessible public transportation, and safer pedestrian pathways."
He says reproductive decisions "should be left to women and their doctors," calls healthcare "a basic human right," and says Ohio must keep a strong Medicaid program.
He says the opioid crisis will need bold solutions, including holistic ways to connect citizens with "life affirming activities and opportunities."
He supports "fair, fully-funded, and safe public schools for all" and says education quality should not depend on zip code.

oh-hd11-2026-kaeser-shawn.name: Shawn Kaeser
oh-hd11-2026-kaeser-shawn.bio: Shawn Kaeser has been a teacher in Dublin for 32 years.

positions.stance: Calls for a "reset for Ohio's schools," including a focus on academic content, more books and fewer screens, eliminating grade inflation, and prioritizing regular attendance.
Says "Taxes are too high" and supports reducing government spending, reforming property tax, and lowering taxes.
Says state policy should lower costs and make Ohio affordable, supporting housing accessibility, energy independence, and "Protecting Seniors and Young Families."

oh-hd11-2026-lett-crystal.name: Crystal Lett
oh-hd11-2026-lett-crystal.bio: Crystal Lett has been the State Representative for Ohio's 11th House District since January 2025, and she previously worked as Recruitment Director at LEAD Ohio, Ohio Program Director of Red Wine & Blue, and a case manager at North Central Mental Health.

positions.stance: She says the Statehouse needs legislators who will push back against attacks on democracy, and she pledges: "I will fight to ensure that Ohioans have representation that fights for the people."
She supports fully funded public education, saying "We MUST invest in our youth," and opposes censoring teachers and banning books.
She wants to restructure the health insurance market so all Ohioans can afford coverage, and to "fully fund and expand public programs like Medicare, Medicaid, and CHIP."
She says quality child care costs more than many families can afford and is hard to find, which pushes parents, especially women, into "impossible economic decisions."

She supports investing in clean, affordable energy and grid modernization to lower costs and create jobs, and says data centers should "pay their fair share" instead of ratepayers covering their energy use.

oh-hd12-2026-stewart-brian.name: Brian Stewart
oh-hd12-2026-stewart-brian.bio: Brian Stewart is the State Representative for Ohio's 12th House District, an Iraq War Army veteran, and the owner of a law practice in Circleville; he previously served as Pickaway County Commissioner and on the Ashville Village Council.

positions.stance: Says he has managed tax dollars in a fiscally conservative way, passing balanced budgets as county commissioner and cutting taxes every year as State Representative, including income tax cuts.
Says he is working to bring job creation across the 12th District, partly by expanding broadband internet to rural communities.
Says he will stand for "pro-life protections for the unborn, 2nd Amendment rights, religious liberty, freedom of speech," a strong national defense, and border security.
States "State government should treat local governments as the partners they are" and says he works with local officials to help meet local needs.

oh-sc-2026-0101-hawkins-daniel.name: Daniel R. Hawkins
oh-sc-2026-0101-hawkins-daniel.bio: Dan Hawkins is a Justice of the Ohio Supreme Court. Before that, he was a Franklin County Court of Common Pleas judge, a Franklin County Municipal Court Environmental Division judge, and an assistant prosecuting attorney in Franklin County, where he directed the Special Victims Unit.

oh-sc-2026-0101-zayas-marilyn.name: Marilyn Zayas
oh-sc-2026-0101-zayas-marilyn.bio: Marilyn Zayas is a judge on Ohio's First District Court of Appeals; she previously worked as an IT manager at Procter & Gamble and practiced law in the private and public sectors, including at her own firm.

oh-sc-2026-0102-brunner-jennifer.name: Jennifer Brunner
oh-sc-2026-0102-brunner-jennifer.bio: Jennifer Brunner is a Justice of the Supreme Court of Ohio and previously served as a judge of Ohio's Tenth District Court of Appeals, a Franklin County Common Pleas Court judge, Ohio Secretary of State, and an attorney in private practice.

oh-sc-2026-0102-o-donnell-colleen.name: Colleen O'Donnell
oh-sc-2026-0102-o-donnell-colleen.bio: Colleen O'Donnell was most recently a U.S. Immigration Judge in Laredo, Texas, and before that was a Franklin County Common Pleas Court judge for nearly a decade; she has also worked at the Public Utilities Commission of Ohio, as an Assistant Attorney General, as a federal court clerk, and in private practice.

oh-sd03-2026-baker-stacie.name: Stacie A. Baker
oh-sd03-2026-baker-stacie.bio: Stacie Baker is a three-term at-large Reynoldsburg City Council member and the council's current President Pro Tempore. He also chairs its Finance Committee and is Reynoldsburg's representative on the West Licking County Joint Fire District Board.

positions.stance: Says working families "deserve pay that keeps up with the cost of living" and that he is fighting to raise wages and protect workers across Ohio.
"Committed to fully funding Ohio’s public schools and supporting teachers."
Says access to mental health care and social services "should not depend on your zip code" and that he will "expand funding for community-based programs."
"Stacie will push for affordable housing development across District 3."
Supports "building a future-ready workforce through vocational training, apprenticeships, and partnerships with local employers."

oh-sd03-2026-reynolds-michele.name: Michele Reynolds
oh-sd03-2026-reynolds-michele.bio: Michele Reynolds has been the Ohio State Senator for District 3 since her election in 2022; she was previously a Madison Township Trustee and describes herself as a third-generation business owner, a nonprofit CEO and a licensed Realtor.

positions.stance: Lists "Creating Affordable Housing Solutions" as a commitment, citing her role chairing the Senate Select Committee on Housing and bills on property tax relief, housing funds and eviction records.
Lists "Expanding Economic Opportunity" as a commitment, citing passage of Ohio's 2.75% flat tax and bills including a family caregiving tax credit and the Tithing Protection Act.
Lists "Strengthening Ohio's Workforce" as a commitment, citing the Child Care Cred Program and a bill requiring certain construction industry employers to use E-verify.
Lists "Improving Public Safety and Criminal Justice Reform" as a commitment, citing bills for school panic alarms, app store parental controls and revised community control sanctions.
Lists "Increasing Access to Justice" as a commitment, citing her seat on the Ohio Access to Justice Foundation board and a bill to set up a housing legal defense fund.

oh-sd15-2026-humphrey-latyna.name: Latyna M. Humphrey
oh-sd15-2026-humphrey-latyna.bio: Latyna M. Humphrey is the State Representative for Ohio's 2nd House District.

positions.stance: Says "it is important that we continue creating constant spaces for at risk youth to be heard and supported."
Lists housing among the priorities she is "continuing to focus on"; her About page names "housing access" as a policy priority.
Lists workforce development among the priorities she is "continuing to focus on."
Lists "economic opportunities" among the priorities she is "continuing to focus on."
Lists childcare among the priorities she is "continuing to focus on"; her About page names "child care affordability" as a policy priority.

oh-sd25-2026-demora-bill.name: Bill DeMora
oh-sd25-2026-demora-bill.bio: Bill DeMora is a Democratic Ohio state senator finishing his first term, representing a district that includes Clintonville, Upper Arlington, Grandview Heights, the Hilltop and Ohio State's campus.

positions.stance: Cosponsored "The Drink Spiking" bill requiring bars and restaurants to give customers date rape drug testing devices free of charge, to help deter date rape.
Worked with Sen. Blessing on a proposed law to repeal the existing Ohio law that allows a minor to get married.
Urged the Ohio Department of Rehabilitation and Correction to ensure "humane, safe and lawful conditions" for people held by ICE at the Butler County Jail.
Has "fought for safety protections for nurses on the job."
Has fought "to respect the will of the people for voting to make cannabis legal."

oh-sd25-2026-roberts-don.name: Don Roberts
oh-sd25-2026-roberts-don.bio: Don Roberts is an attorney and Air Force veteran with more than 20 years of legal experience, and a former Legal Aid supervising attorney and police officer.

positions.stance: Says "everyone deserves a second chance" and supports expanding expungement eligibility so more people can access jobs, housing, and education opportunities.
Supports "fair and balanced custody policies that prioritize the best interests of the child while ensuring both parents are treated equally under the law."
Focused on solutions that "support small businesses, promote job growth, and put more money back in the pockets of working families."

oh-sos-2026-russo-allison.name: Allison Russo
oh-sos-2026-russo-allison.bio: Allison Russo has served four terms in the Ohio House of Representatives, including as Minority Leader, and is a senior director for a federally-qualified small business after more than 20 years working in health care policy.

positions.stance: She says the Secretary of State's job includes ensuring "our elections remain fair, secure, and accessible."
She says Ohioans deserve a Chief Elections Officer who believes "voters should choose their politicians, not the other way around."
She says she is running "to restore trust in our elections."
She says she is running to "protect your personal data."
She says she is running to "make sure government is accountable to the people it serves."

oh-sos-2026-sprague-robert.name: Robert Sprague
oh-sos-2026-sprague-robert.bio: Robert Sprague's campaign site says he has worked in engineering and finance and has served as State Treasurer, managing Ohio taxpayer dollars.

positions.stance: Will work with the Trump Administration to get federal citizenship data and verify citizenship when people register to vote, before they are placed on voter rolls.
Will build on in-person photo ID "by requiring photo ID for mail-in voting, the same requirement expected of those who vote in-person."
Calls drop boxes outdated, Covid-era leftovers that are vulnerable to ballot harvesting and fraud and not worth the cost to secure, and says he will eliminate them.
Wants a bipartisan panel of election board officials to review all processes and chain-of-custody requirements after every election to make sure laws were followed.
"Under Robert Sprague, Ohio will be a paper ballot state." Any voting machine must produce a verifiable, auditable paper trail.

oh-treas-2026-edwards-jay.name: Jay Edwards
oh-treas-2026-edwards-jay.bio: Jay Edwards is a former member of the Ohio House of Representatives, where he served as Chairman of the House Finance Committee.

positions.stance: As Treasurer, he says he will bring a "numbers-first approach" to the state's checkbook so every dollar is spent "wisely, transparently, and in a way that benefits Ohioans first."
"As our next Treasurer, I will keep politics out of our investments & keep those dollars in our local communities."

oh-treas-2026-walsh-seth.name: Seth Walsh
oh-treas-2026-walsh-seth.bio: Seth Walsh is a Cincinnati City Council member and serves on the Cincinnati Retirement System Board of Trustees. He previously led the Sedamsville Community Development Corporation and the College Hill Community Urban Redevelopment Corporation.

positions.stance: He says he "will not make new investments in the State of Israel or any other country" and will put Ohio's funds into community banks and A-rated or higher bonds instead of BBB-rated bonds.
He says he will use the Treasurer's investment tools and partnerships "to help entrepreneurs gain access to capital and build lasting businesses."
He says he will "work to expand partnerships that support affordable housing and help first-time homebuyers."
He says Ohio's $4.8 billion in unclaimed funds should go back to their owners and not be used for legislators' projects, and he wants claiming them to be easier.
He says he will appoint "qualified, diverse, and independent leaders who put retirees first" to pension boards and will call for transparency and oversight of retirement funds.

S6OH00163.name: Sherrod Brown
S6OH00163.bio: Former U.S. Senator from Ohio, born and raised in Mansfield.

positions.stance: "It's time to ban health insurance companies from denying the care your doctor says you need," and fine insurers that deny claims.
"Let's make it illegal for drug companies to charge Americans more than they do in other countries."
Require data centers "to pay the full cost of their utilities so your bills don't go up," and let Ohioans decide whether data centers are built locally.
Cap "how much utility companies can raise your rates" so bills are affordable and predictable.
Ban members of Congress and their spouses from trading stocks, and bar members from becoming lobbyists after they leave office.

S6OH00304.name: Jon Husted
S6OH00304.bio: U.S. Senator from Ohio (appointed January 2025); former Ohio lieutenant governor, secretary of state, and Ohio House speaker.

S6OH00395.name: Gregory Lee Levy
S6OH00395.bio: Community organizer, U.S. military veteran, and mover from Akron.

positions.stance: "We are building a socialist movement to end the rule of the billionaires once and for all."
Take the 100 biggest corporations into public ownership; enact a national rent cap at 20% of income, single-payer health care, and free public education through college.
"Outlaw corporate lobbying and political donations" and move to abolish the Senate and Supreme Court, "transferring their powers to more democratic and accountable bodies."
Calls for "full payment of reparations to Black Americans for slavery and Jim Crow dictatorship" and placing police departments under direct community control.
"Slash the Pentagon budget by 90%," dismantle U.S. military bases abroad, and dissolve NATO, the CIA and AFRICOM.

S6OH00429.name: William Redpath
S6OH00429.bio: Certified public accountant and retired business valuation professional; former chair of the Libertarian National Committee.

positions.stance: Calls U.S. participation in the war against Iran "clearly unconstitutional" and says Donald Trump should be impeached and removed for not seeking Congressional approval.
"The United States should end all tariffs on imported goods and services, regardless of the policies of other nations."
Endorses allowing all immigration except "criminals, terrorists, the seriously ill, or others who would harm the life, liberty, and property of people here."
Favors a BRAC-style Social Security reform commission, paying Medicare enrollees in cash, and turning Medicaid over to the states over ten years.
Calls for eliminating the Departments of Education and Housing & Urban Development and ending all corporate welfare and farm subsidies.
